prediction.likelyOutcome: Barham should recover at least the $163,000 court-appraiser floor for the physical taking, and has a genuine, better-than-even shot at a materially larger jury award on the theory that the Threel Road easement extinguishment and loss of the dealership's main entrance caused compensable consequential damages, given that summary judgment on that issue was already denied. The ultimate size of any enhancement is unquantified in the current record because no appraisal or expert valuation of the access loss has been supplied.

issues.label: Compensability of Threel Road Ingress-Egress Easement Extinguishment
Carmel's Traffic-Flow-Rule Defense to Access Compensation

outcome.description: After a May 2022 jury trial the Marion Circuit Court entered judgment on a $2.4 million verdict for Barham and denied Carmel's motions to correct error, for new trial, and for remittitur. The Court of Appeals reversed on October 30, 2023, holding Barham had no compensable easement interest in Threel Road (already extinguished in the County Line condemnation) and that the access change was non-compensable under the ingress-egress and traffic-flow rules, and remanded with instructions to grant Carmel partial summary judgment on that issue.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
